output.review_comment:
The overweight check and the round-half-up fix look fine. Consider `decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP` to avoid float edge cases.

The problem is the tier-boundary change from `<=` to `<`. By the PR's own account, it was made "only so that test_two_kilo_parcel_zone1 passes," and it contradicts the docstring, which says tier limits are inclusive. The change isn't limited to 2.0 kg. It moves every exact-boundary weight (0.5 kg and every other limit) up to the next, more expensive tier. That's a real pricing change, and only one boundary has a test.

The teammate says the tests encode the agreed carrier spec, but the docstring says otherwise, so one of them is wrong. This conflict should go to the carrier partnerships team, not be settled by changing the code to match one test. If exclusive limits are right, update the docstring and add tests at every tier boundary. If inclusive limits are right, the test is wrong and should be flagged rather than satisfied. The overweight and rounding fixes could be split into their own PR and merged now.
